dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Nam, do your grandparents still live in the village?
dialogue.reading: ˈnɑːm, duː jʊr ˈɡrænpɛrənts ˈstɪl ˈlɪv ɪn ðə ˈvɪlɪdʒ?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Yes, they still live there. But the village is different now.
dialogue.reading: ˈjɛs, ðeɪ ˈstɪl ˈlɪv ˈðɛr. bʌt ðə ˈvɪlɪdʒ ɪz ˈdɪfərənt ˈnaʊ.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: There are new roads and shops. Children don't play by the river any more.
dialogue.reading: ðɛr ər ˈnuː ˈroʊdz ənd ˈʃɑːps. ˈtʃɪldrən ˈdoʊnt ˈpleɪ baɪ ðə ˈrɪvər ˈɛni ˈmɔːr.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: That's sad. Do you still see your childhood friends?
dialogue.reading: ðæts ˈsæd. duː juː ˈstɪl ˈsiː jʊr ˈtʃaɪldhʊd ˈfrɛndz?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Some of them. My friend from kindergarten moved away to Chiang Mai, but we keep in touch.
dialogue.reading: ˈsʌm əv ðɛm. maɪ ˈfrɛnd frəm ˈkɪndərɡɑːrtən ˈmuːvd əˈweɪ tə ˈtʃjɑːŋ ˈmaɪ, bʌt wiː ˈkiːp ɪn ˈtʌtʃ.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: That's nice. I lost touch with most of my school friends.
dialogue.reading: ðæts ˈnaɪs. aɪ ˈlɔːst ˈtʌtʃ wɪð ˈmoʊst əv maɪ ˈskuːl ˈfrɛndz.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Does your family still live in your village in Canada?
dialogue.reading: dʌz jʊr ˈfæməli ˈstɪl ˈlɪv ɪn jʊr ˈvɪlɪdʒ ɪn ˈkænədə?

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: No, they don't live there any longer. My mother moved away to Toronto.
dialogue.reading: ˈnoʊ, ðeɪ ˈdoʊnt ˈlɪv ˈðɛr ˈɛni ˈlɔːŋər. maɪ ˈmʌðər ˈmuːvd əˈweɪ tə təˈrɑːntoʊ.
